$comment: Which one-time code, if any, an SMS or notification carries (OtpExtractor.kt, T-0135).
A text carries a code only when it names one: one of `keywords` occurs (case-insensitive,
whole words). Candidates are 4-8 digits standing alone, an optional letter prefix such
as Google's `G-` allowed, or two groups of three joined by one hyphen or space
(`123-456` -> `123456`). A candidate touching other number syntax is not a code: preceded
by a currency sign, `#`, `+`, `/`, or a digit and hyphen; followed by `/`, or by `.` `,`
`-` `:` and a digit (decimals, dates, times, phone numbers). Of what is left, the one
nearest the first keyword wins (ties: the earlier). `code: null` when there is none.
Only the code leaves the phone; the text it came from never does.

cases.name: Google's G- prefix
cases.text: G-123456 is your Google verification code.

cases.name: code before the keyword
cases.text: 123456 is your Instagram code. Don't share it.
